findings.attribution: The -1 sentinel at S+0x38 is overwritten by the conversion chain, not by the slot-0x64e0518 callee. The conversion body 0x5cead40 makes no store through its argument at all (its only stores are four stack slots); it tail-jumps at 0x5ceae3e to the setter body 0x5cea7c0 with rcx = &[S+0x20], rdx = the converted value and rdi = the wheel object at handle+sel+0x50. The setter stores the value at 0x5cea8c1 (mov [r14+0x18], r12 with r14 = &[S+0x20], i.e. S+0x38) and at 0x5cea8c5 ([r14+0x10], i.e. S+0x30).
findings.builder_inputs: Builder 0x5cf2150(rdi = S, rsi = duration seconds, edx = duration nanoseconds, rcx = descriptor static 0x644dc28). It calls the base-value body 0x5c842e0 with edi = 1 (sites 0x5cf216f and, on the overflow fallback, 0x5cf21b6; the fallback adds 946080000 to the re-read seconds). 0x5c842e0 forwards that 1 untouched as the clock id of the GLOB_DAT slot 0x64e1248 (clock_gettime) and returns its (sec, nsec) pair, unwrap-trapping on error (message at 0x949294) and trapping if nsec >= 1000000000. The builder forms deadline sec = clock sec + duration sec (checked; on overflow the fallback path runs) and deadline nsec = clock nsec + duration nsec normalised into [0, 1e9) with carry into the seconds. It calls the accessor behind slot 0x64e0848 (0x5cf2b50) with the descriptor: the accessor returns rax in {0, 1} (strong/weak flag) and rdx = the calling thread's current handle pointer (read from the TLS cell at fs:-0x1130+0x10) after a lock xadd refcount increment on it, and the builder asserts [handle+sel+0x90] != 1000000000 (sel from rax bit 0) through the same timers-disabled trap. Stores (0x5cf2261..0x5cf226f): [S+0x60] = deadline sec (qword), [S+0x68] = deadline nsec (dword), [S+0x0] = accessor flag, [S+0x8] = handle, [S+0x10] = 2. The conversion body consumes exactly the pair: [S+0x60] as an integer seconds count (incremented on the nsec carry arm, never dereferenced) and dword [S+0x68] as its nanosecond part - a (sec, nsec) deadline, differenced against the handle's stored (sec, nsec) at [handle+sel+0x88]/[handle+sel+0x90].
findings.conversion_contract: 0x5cead40(rdi = &[S+0x10], rsi = [S+0x60] seconds, edx = dword [S+0x68] nanoseconds). It reads the handle [S+0x18], selects the table offset from byte [S+0x10] (nonzero -> 0x160, zero -> 0x240), and traps through the assert-fail callee behind slot 0x64df770 if dword [handle+sel+0x90] == 1000000000 - the 115-byte message at 0x94ca6b (timers disabled) - at 0x5cead6a and again at 0x5ceaddd after the difference call. The (sec, nsec) pair is adjusted: nsec >= 999000001 -> sec += 1 (overflow trap at 0x5ceae5c, "overflow when adding duration to instant"), nsec -= 999000001; else nsec += 999999. It then calls the difference body 0x5c84210 with a stack descriptor {sec, nsec, [handle+sel+0x88], [handle+sel+0x90]} whose tail doubles as the second operand, computing (sec, nsec) - (handle sec, handle nsec) into {sign, diff sec, diff nsec} (body 0x5c84210, swap-recursive on A < B, panic "overflow in Duration::new"). The converted value is diff_sec * 1000 + (diff_nsec * 1125899907 >> 50) + carry (a millisecond-shaped count), forced to 0 when the difference sign qword is nonzero, and saturated at 0xfffffffffffffffd. Return is the tail jump into the setter.
findings.normalise_negative: Body 0x5cf1d70 is called by the predicate at 0x5cf2e01, before the sentinel store at 0x5cf2e1e, and on the [S+0x10] == 2 path it returns immediately (its first check is dword [rdi] == 2). In general it writes only through the handle it drops (two lock decq stores) and never through its argument struct, so it cannot be the writer either.
findings.postcall_negative: Body 0x5ce91b0 (slot 0x64e0518), called by the predicate on &[S+0x40] after the conversion returns, cannot reach the sentinel: relative to its argument the sentinel sits at -0x8, and the body's complete argument-store census is offsets {0x0, 0x8, 0x10} only (a once-cell state cmpxchg at +0x10, a pair store at +0x0/+0x8, a contention steal at +0x0 and an xchg at +0x10). Its exception-handling pads add exactly one further argument store - a lock cmpxchg at 0x5ce9489 on the same +0x10 state word, on a cleanup path that jumps back into the main contention flow - and three lock decq stores through the global counter pointer loaded from slot 0x64dfe90 (0x5ce9296, 0x5ce9350, 0x5ce946b). No store anywhere in the body uses a negative displacement from the argument.
findings.predicate_flow: Predicate 0x5cf2d30 on the non-TLS, [S+0x10] == 2 path: refcount-increments [S+0x8], calls 0x5cf1d70 on &[S+0x10] (no-op for tag 2), then stores the entry fields itself - [S+0x10] = derived flag, [S+0x18] = handle, [S+0x20..0x30] = 0, [S+0x30] = 0, [S+0x38] = -1 at 0x5cf2e1e, [S+0x40] = 0, [S+0x50] = 0, byte [S+0x58] = 0 - calls the conversion, re-checks the handle fields, calls 0x5ce91b0 on &[S+0x40], and only then reads [S+0x38] for its return rule (1 iff != -1; 0 iff == -1 and byte [S+0x58] == 0; -1 with byte [S+0x58] != 0 takes the timer-error unwind). The same eight field stores repeat in the timer-error landing pad at 0x5cf2f99 (the sentinel re-stored at 0x5cf2fb1) before the pad drops the entry through 0x5cf1d10 and resumes the unwind - a cleanup re-initialisation, not a second decision path.
findings.setter_contract: 0x5cea7c0(rdi = wheel object at handle+sel+0x50, rsi = adjusted seconds, rdx = converted value, rcx = &[S+0x20] entry). Entry byte-locks the wheel (lock cmpxchg [rdi], 1 at 0x5cea7d8); on contention it waits via slot 0x64e01f8 -> 0x5bb59d0 with a 1000000000 timeout and re-reads the entry. Before the flag test it unlinks or bucket-inserts an entry whose value slot is already set: level index from bsr((value xor [wheel+0x10]) | 0x3f) clamped to 0xffffffffe, bucket = [wheel+0x8] + level * 0x410, insert body 0x5ce29a0; an out-of-range level traps at the wheel Location static 0x64c6a48 (path string at 0x446310, line 130 col 17). The decision is the byte at [wheel+0x30], loaded at 0x5cea881 - see the decision table. After a direct store it calls the insert body 0x5cf6880 (rdi = &[wheel+0x8], rsi = entry), which links the entry and returns a (rax, rdx) pair; the setter then rebinds r14 to the rdx object at 0x5cea8d5 and processes that returned entry (its own flag byte and value slot, a callback through [rdx+0x8]) - stores after 0x5cea8d5 are on that other object, not on S.

open_edges: The source identity of the wheel byte at [wheel+0x30] (the flag the setter tests at 0x5cea881): which writer sets it, and on what event, is not traced in this packet; only its three-way effect on the entry is pinned.

The runtime contents of the handle fields [handle+sel+0x88]/[handle+sel+0x90] (the stored (sec, nsec) the deadline is differenced against) and of the globals behind the TLS accessor cell - runtime data, not statically decidable from the artifact.

The insert body 0x5cf6880's returned (rax, rdx) object semantics beyond the setter's use of it (an already-due entry handed back for immediate processing); its internals are exported but its producer conditions are not censused here.
Who re-invokes the gates to reach checker state 3 and the provenance of [record+0x1d8] before its first checker_a call (open edge 4 of #2613) remain open.
